metric_notes.avg: 90-day average: 155.94 €/MWh. Up +68.1% vs the previous period (92.77 €/MWh): a clear upward trend from August (≈123 €/MWh weekly) to the week of Nov 2 (222.4 €/MWh).
metric_notes.min: Lowest price in the window: 0 €/MWh on Oct 18 at 11:00. 21 days with prices ≤ 0.001 €/MWh (~24% of the period): wind keeps giving energy away even in winter.
metric_notes.max: Absolute maximum: 380 €/MWh on Nov 4 at 20:00. The most expensive day was Nov 4, with an average of 257.6 €/MWh.

verdict.label: NEUTRAL
verdict.title: No fixed-tariff benchmark this period
verdict.body: There are no recent fixed (24h) tariffs in the database to compare against, so we cannot say whether PVPC or a flat tariff saves money right now. The estimated PVPC price for the period is 0.211 €/kWh. With gas-driven peaks of 380 €/MWh in November evening hours, anyone on a recent fixed tariff is probably saving; if you are on PVPC, shift consumption to the zero-price windows.

factors.title: Gas drives the evening peaks
factors.body: Heating demand pushes gas (MIBGAS) prices up exactly when electricity use peaks: the 18–22h slot in November keeps hitting new highs, with a 380 €/MWh spike on Nov 4 at 20:00.
factors.impact: Direct impact: +68% period average vs the previous quarter

factors.title: 21 days at zero or negative price
factors.body: Wind production pushed the pool price to 0 €/MWh (or below) on a quarter of the days in the period, even in late autumn. The cheapest day was Oct 18, averaging just 76.3 €/MWh.
factors.impact: Direct impact: up to -100% in windy slots

factors.title: This time the night doesn't pay off
factors.body: Normally the off-peak (night) slot is the cheapest. This period it's the opposite: off-peak 0.217 €/kWh vs mid-peak 0.201 and peak 0.209. With nighttime heating demand and no solar output, charging your home or car 'at night' no longer guarantees savings.
factors.impact: Direct impact: off-peak costs ~8% more than mid-peak this period

golden_rule: In winter the map changes: chase windy zero-price days instead of a time slot, and avoid November's 18–22h window at all costs.
